issuing_body: Minnesota Office of the Legislative Auditor
title: Department of Human Services: Behavioral Health Administration Grants
conclusion: OLA concluded BHA did not comply with most requirements tested and did not have adequate internal controls over grant funds.

integrity_issue.claim: During the audit, OLA identified a number of documents that BHA either backdated or created after the audit began; OLA said it could not fully rely on that documentation.
integrity_issue.locator: PDF p.2, lines 43-63; visually confirmed on page screenshot
integrity_issue.qualification: This is a serious audit-evidence integrity issue. It is not by itself a criminal charge, conviction, or proof that the documents were created to facilitate theft.

selected_findings: Unjustified or insufficiently documented single-source grants.
Grant agreements lacking required statutory-authority citations.
Late grant amendments and payments for work before fully executed grant agreements.
Two grantees were overpaid a total of $41,803.
No competitive-bid process for certain mental-health provider-supervision grants.
Prior findings remained unresolved regarding progress reports, monitoring visits, financial reconciliations, and grantee-performance evaluations.
Payments were made for some costs not incurred or not properly supported by source documentation.
The Legislature had not established an oversight mechanism for certain payments to legislatively named entities.
Staff described poor leadership practices and insufficient grant-management training.

money.notes: OLA tested 55 of 57 grant agreements to 18 grantees in the relevant payment comparison and found two grantees overpaid a combined $41,803 on two reimbursement requests. This is not a $41,803 criminal-fraud finding.
money.source_locator: report p.19 / PDF p.24, lines 758-768; visually confirmed on screenshot

source_locators.summary_findings: PDF pp.8-11 / OLA HTML report summary

does_not_support: The audit does not establish a statewide amount of behavioral-health grant fraud.
The $41,803 audit-identified overpayment is not a criminal stolen-funds total.
Backdating/creating documents after audit commencement is not, from this audit alone, a criminal adjudication against BHA staff.
The annual grant-expense figures are program spending, not fraud losses.
Audit findings involving unsupported or not-incurred costs require recovery/reconciliation follow-up and should not automatically be labeled intentional fraud.
